Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "Gulliver's Travels", "unit": 31, "heading": "CHAPTER X.", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en99-031-0012", "target": "Я распространялся ещё о многих других предметах, которые естественное желание бесконечной жизни и подлунного счастья легко мне подсказывало. Когда я кончил и суть моей речи была, как и прежде, передана остальному обществу, между ними завязался долгий разговор на языке страны, не без некоторого смеха на мой счёт. Наконец тот же господин, что был моим переводчиком, сказал, «что остальные поручили ему поправить меня в нескольких заблуждениях, в которые я впал по общей немощи человеческой природы и по этой причине менее за них ответствен. Что эта порода [[I]]струльдбругов[[/I]] свойственна только их стране, ибо подобных людей нет ни в Бальнибарби, ни в Японии, где он имел честь быть послом от его величества и где нашёл, что тамошним жителям очень трудно поверить в возможность такого явления; и по моему изумлению, когда он впервые заговорил со мной об этом, видно, что я воспринял это как нечто совершенно новое и едва ли вероятное. Что в двух вышеупомянутых королевствах, где он за время своего пребывания много беседовал с людьми, он заметил, что долгая жизнь — всеобщее желание и мечта человечества. Что всякий, у кого одна нога в могиле, непременно удерживает другую изо всех сил. Что самый старый всё ещё надеется прожить хоть день лишний и смотрит на смерть как на величайшее зло, от которого природа всегда побуждает его отступать. Только на этом острове Лаггнегг жажда жизни не так пылка, благодаря постоянному примеру [[I]]струльдбругов[[/I]] перед глазами.", "source_sha256": "29b466795d4868fb2bcfeb2dc24ef7a8e3dc8f83e9873a2f1e680c7a78287a57", "target_id": "ru-en99-031-0012", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "efcef2c097eb3ebac5c897c48a566469075e812086111a3412d7eb6d77b664f6"}, {"source_id": "en99-031-0013", "target": "«Что придуманный мною образ жизни неразумен и несправедлив, потому что предполагает вечную юность, здоровье и силу, на какие ни один человек не может быть столь глуп, чтобы надеяться, сколь бы ни были безрассудны его желания. Что вопрос поэтому состоит не в том, пожелал ли бы человек быть всегда в расцвете юности, в довольстве и здравии, но в том, как он проводил бы вечную жизнь при всех обычных невзгодах, которые приносит с собой старость. Ибо хотя немногие признаются в желании бессмертия на таких тяжких условиях, однако в двух упомянутых королевствах, Бальнибарби и Японии, он заметил, что каждый желает отсрочить смерть ещё на некоторое время, как бы поздно она ни приближалась; и он редко слышал о человеке, который умер бы охотно, разве что его побудила к тому крайняя скорбь или пытка. И он спросил меня, не наблюдал ли я той же всеобщей склонности в странах, которые объехал, равно как и в моей собственной».»", "source_sha256": "8db66be0303b38fdc0960d159cf6ca2660d2733088c9f1bdb2d439b653a949cc", "target_id": "ru-en99-031-0013", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "6a93f78c08942bc5ff5388a8fde63dac9e2807d80330337c8fd1bf1dca76d474"}], "source_language": "English", "part": 3, "book": null, "chapter": 10, "role": "PRINCIPAL_CHAPTER"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en99-031-0014", "tag": "p", "text": "After this preface, he gave me a particular account of the [[I]]struldbrugs[[/I]] among them. He said, “they commonly acted like mortals till about thirty years old; after which, by degrees, they grew melancholy and dejected, increasing in both till they came to fourscore. This he learned from their own confession: for otherwise, there not being above two or three of that species born in an age, they were too few to form a general observation by. When they came to fourscore years, which is reckoned the extremity of living in this country, they had not only all the follies and infirmities of other old men, but many more which arose from the dreadful prospect of never dying. They were not only opinionative, peevish, covetous, morose, vain, talkative, but incapable of friendship, and dead to all natural affection, which never descended below their grandchildren. Envy and impotent desires are their prevailing passions. But those objects against which their envy seems principally directed, are the vices of the younger sort and the deaths of the old. By reflecting on the former, they find themselves cut off from all possibility of pleasure; and whenever they see a funeral, they lament and repine that others have gone to a harbour of rest to which they themselves never can hope to arrive. They have no remembrance of anything but what they learned and observed in their youth and middle-age, and even that is very imperfect; and for the truth or particulars of any fact, it is safer to depend on common tradition, than upon their best recollections. The least miserable among them appear to be those who turn to dotage, and entirely lose their memories; these meet with more pity and assistance, because they want many bad qualities which abound in others.", "sha256": "7376e69076c14fe0640103a16b8882bd8b9676ee0db25c083ab818d8e82e79e5", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[14]", "source_html_sha256": "5491f44b7dd45870e9bdeea786324295371999ad38cfc71a67c3ef7f653ef5dd", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0015", "tag": "p", "text": "“If a [[I]]struldbrug[[/I]] happen to marry one of his own kind, the marriage is dissolved of course, by the courtesy of the kingdom, as soon as the younger of the two comes to be fourscore; for the law thinks it a reasonable indulgence, that those who are condemned, without any fault of their own, to a perpetual continuance in the world, should not have their misery doubled by the load of a wife.", "sha256": "f7f281c460fe699145e53ab31ef8ed88c0512b10204b4fd7ba49b969c4b5bf40", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[15]", "source_html_sha256": "48d15b39a127cdf96fbef0fd4855af1212526984ff469bcdfd9273d9d3b985dc", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0016", "tag": "p", "text": "“As soon as they have completed the term of eighty years, they are looked on as dead in law; their heirs immediately succeed to their estates; only a small pittance is reserved for their support; and the poor ones are maintained at the public charge. After that period, they are held incapable of any employment of trust or profit; they cannot purchase lands, or take leases; neither are they allowed to be witnesses in any cause, either civil or criminal, not even for the decision of meers and bounds.", "sha256": "7d9e1f2e332cf7421c6a2ec57d4239babce54e061c28324cf5834f3067abdb8a", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[16]", "source_html_sha256": "f127b04e8678d25459aaf5599ffbcb6bf69cb44170114e0b1e09a63a463fcce8", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0017", "tag": "p", "text": "“At ninety, they lose their teeth and hair; they have at that age no distinction of taste, but eat and drink whatever they can get, without relish or appetite. The diseases they were subject to still continue, without increasing or diminishing. In talking, they forget the common appellation of things, and the names of persons, even of those who are their nearest friends and relations. For the same reason, they never can amuse themselves with reading, because their memory will not serve to carry them from the beginning of a sentence to the end; and by this defect, they are deprived of the only entertainment whereof they might otherwise be capable.", "sha256": "0bf3b570ef76b26523e92db378f8b5c62c63fd53288083304388f9eb6af7731f", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[17]", "source_html_sha256": "8b1b99ba80726b54b20e09e542b75f7fcdb62db9f5e45475d032a5d58dde856b", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0018", "tag": "p", "text": "“The language of this country being always upon the flux, the [[I]]struldbrugs[[/I]] of one age do not understand those of another; neither are they able, after two hundred years, to hold any conversation (farther than by a few general words) with their neighbours the mortals; and thus they lie under the disadvantage of living like foreigners in their own country.”", "sha256": "83bdf4838c48093d061e916bf61cf5c46ebe1a23ae0afcbe88f5b28abf429a13", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[18]", "source_html_sha256": "8a6aed966bc13a228e28676645cabb6db6ffef2d7483f14d636b0cb666a7de07", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0019", "tag": "p", "text": "This was the account given me of the [[I]]struldbrugs[[/I]], as near as I can remember. I afterwards saw five or six of different ages, the youngest not above two hundred years old, who were brought to me at several times by some of my friends; but although they were told, “that I was a great traveller, and had seen all the world,” they had not the least curiosity to ask me a question; only desired “I would give them [[I]]slumskudask[[/I]],” or a token of remembrance; which is a modest way of begging, to avoid the law, that strictly forbids it, because they are provided for by the public, although indeed with a very scanty allowance.", "sha256": "633aebd51e71253c9e0ed60db419efa1c9b4280a298e61f09e09c544a944265e", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[19]", "source_html_sha256": "4ad007f05f4a1ef91503f8152141025d167e73d09ca12172286e6372be8348b9", "emphasis_spans": 2, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0020", "tag": "p", "text": "They are despised and hated by all sorts of people. When one of them is born, it is reckoned ominous, and their birth is recorded very particularly so that you may know their age by consulting the register, which, however, has not been kept above a thousand years past, or at least has been destroyed by time or public disturbances. But the usual way of computing how old they are, is by asking them what kings or great persons they can remember, and then consulting history; for infallibly the last prince in their mind did not begin his reign after they were fourscore years old.", "sha256": "7c1c5b45a2e768214e8f3f11afa8269cc0970a791469c5250b3e9efa2f623c1e", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[20]", "source_html_sha256": "c8a37f470de2426b8d9b050fee8c454b35c03eba17ec144c007da7edcbfd4b1c", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0021", "tag": "p", "text": "They were the most mortifying sight I ever beheld; and the women more horrible than the men. Besides the usual deformities in extreme old age, they acquired an additional ghastliness, in proportion to their number of years, which is not to be described; and among half a dozen, I soon distinguished which was the eldest, although there was not above a century or two between them.", "sha256": "75e7e5cb4344c666af79eb1ee9cf006ad289612e58308c8394c2ea7b41664fe5", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[21]", "source_html_sha256": "c666f83eb8beb352e35bc1445b0a633499d51467bae410d751beba7a71ea8df8", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0022", "tag": "p", "text": "The reader will easily believe, that from what I had heard and seen, my keen appetite for perpetuity of life was much abated. I grew heartily ashamed of the pleasing visions I had formed; and thought no tyrant could invent a death into which I would not run with pleasure, from such a life. The king heard of all that had passed between me and my friends upon this occasion, and rallied me very pleasantly; wishing I could send a couple of [[I]]struldbrugs[[/I]] to my own country, to arm our people against the fear of death; but this, it seems, is forbidden by the fundamental laws of the kingdom, or else I should have been well content with the trouble and expense of transporting them.", "sha256": "a416517528d4c091158639a63c8da91e900559e99b0473575ac8144a5118a43e", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[22]", "source_html_sha256": "a0adb540aa4eeca8d7d37590755c090d61fd621225353bad1987b502c85d6758", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-031-0023", "tag": "p", "text": "I could not but agree, that the laws of this kingdom relative to the [[I]]struldbrugs[[/I]] were founded upon the strongest reasons, and such as any other country would be under the necessity of enacting, in the like circumstances. Otherwise, as avarice is the necessary consequence of old age, those immortals would in time become proprietors of the whole nation, and engross the civil power, which, for want of abilities to manage, must end in the ruin of the public.", "sha256": "dbe383e95c4491b3bbf273d52436422d05dd41ff173cdb5daf91b52aa71501d1", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[33]/p[23]", "source_html_sha256": "97d3e523a41fd944981f49556fcbc3d1e84a3409baede85c46cfe507ab8dc03a", "emphasis_spans": 1, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}], "format_retry_instruction": "Previous response failed strict validation: AssertionError: EMPHASIS_MARKER_COUNT.
